subject: Warning about transformed left-hand-side, in censoring model

messages.author: 275b133a3506805a
messages.subject: Warning about transformed left-hand-side, in censoring model
parts:
Hi all,

I'm building a model involving a kind of censoring. I am getting the
following warning:

Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains
a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant
of the Jacobian of the transform.
Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
gap ~ lognormal_log(...)

and I'm trying to work out if it's important in this case or not. (I
know the parser can't always tell if this warning is definitely
needed.)

My model is below. It involves K individuals who each sample a value
but only the minimum of the K values is observed. (We also get to
observe k, i.e. which one won.) It has a lot in common with censored
data, but the censoring point moves.

Any suggestions re increment_log_prob(), please?

Thanks
Dan



data {
int<lower=0> N; // num observations
int<lower=1> K; // num individuals
real timepos[N]; // timepos of event n
int<lower=1,upper=K> individ[N]; // who is responsible for event n
}
parameters {
real<lower=0> excesstimepos[N,K-1]; // for non-observed param, the
excess >0, making it up to the time they "would have" called next.
implicit uniform prior combines with log-gaussian on gap to create
truncated distribs.
real gap_self_mean;
real<lower=0> gap_self_stdv;
}
model {
real prevtimes[K];
real currtimes[K];
real gap;

// priors
gap_self_mean ~ normal(-0.7, 1.0);
gap_self_stdv ~ inv_gamma(1.0, 1.0);

// initialise the main loop
for(k in 1:K){
prevtimes[k] <- timepos[1] - 0.5;
}

for(n in 1:N){
// ok, so timepos[n] is correct for individ k. for the others,
they're lower-bounded by it.
// the moveable bounds are implemented by adding a
zero-bounded hidden variable.
for(k in 1:K){
if(individ[n]==k){
currtimes[k] <- timepos[n];
}else if(individ[n]< k){
currtimes[k] <- timepos[n] + excesstimepos[n, k];
}else{
currtimes[k] <- timepos[n] + excesstimepos[n, k-1];
}
}//k

// now we place distributions over the time gaps, e.g.
independent or not.
// keep this as a separate loop over k, because might use
distribs that depend on all of them.
for(k in 1:K){
gap <- currtimes[k] - prevtimes[k];
gap ~ lognormal(gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv);
}//k

// finally we prepare for the next iteration
for(k in 1:K){
prevtimes[k] <- currtimes[k];
}//k
}//n
}//model

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Warning about transformed left-hand-side, in censoring model
parts:
I compressed the model so I could read it on one screen.

data {
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=1> K;
real timepos[N];
int<lower=1,upper=K> individ[N];

}
parameters {
real<lower=0> excesstimepos[N,K-1];

real gap_self_mean;
real<lower=0> gap_self_stdv;
}
model {
real prevtimes[K];
real currtimes[K];
real gap;

gap_self_mean ~ normal(-0.7, 1.0);
gap_self_stdv ~ inv_gamma(1.0, 1.0);
for (k in 1:K)

prevtimes[k] <- timepos[1] - 0.5;
for (n in 1:N) {

for (k in 1:K) {
if (individ[n] == k) {
currtimes[k] <- timepos[n];
} else if (individ[n] < k) {

currtimes[k] <- timepos[n] + excesstimepos[n, k];
} else {
currtimes[k] <- timepos[n] + excesstimepos[n, k-1];
}
}
for (k in 1:K) {

gap <- currtimes[k] - prevtimes[k];
gap ~ lognormal(gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv);
}
for (k in 1:K)

prevtimes[k] <- currtimes[k];
}
}

For clarity (and a bit of speed), I'd rewrite the loop to be:

for (n in 1:N) {
for (k in 1:(individ[n] - 1))
curtimes[k] <- timepos[n] + excesstimespos[n,k];
curtimes[indivd[n]] <- timepos[n];
for (k in (individ[n] + 1):K)
curtimes[k] <- timepos[n] + excesstimepos[n,k-1];
}

timepos is data, whereas excesstimepos is a parameter. This makes
it clear that each excesstimepos gets used exactly once.

What's confusing me about whether you need a Jacobian is that
you reassign prevtimes to currtimes, so that you get a rolling
accumulation of excesstimepos, which is a parameter. So what
you need to do is work out the entire mapping from excesstimepos to
all the N * K gap values and make sure that transform
has a constant Jacobian. Hopefully someone else who's better at calc
can give you the answer. It should simplify because the Jacobian's
going to be lower triangular, so even if you have to calculate it it
shouldn't be too bad.

Lacking help on the calculus, you can try simulating data from
the model and see if you can recover it.

You probably want to vectorize that big lognormal for efficiency
given that they all have the same variance. That'll provide a huge
speedup.

Even just defining curtimes and prevtimes as vectors and replacing

for (k in 1:K) {

gap <- currtimes[k] - prevtimes[k];
gap ~ lognormal(gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv);
}

with

currtimes - prevtimes ~ lognormal(gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv);

should give you a substantial speedup.

And you can replace

for (k in 1:K)
prevtimes[k] <- timepos[1] - 0.5;

with

prevtimes <- rep_vector(timepos[1] - 0.5, K);

and

for (k in 1:K)
prevtimes[k] <- currtimes[k];

with

prevtimes <- currtimes;

- Bob

messages.author: 275b133a3506805a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Warning about transformed left-hand-side, in censoring model
parts:
Hi,

Thanks for the feedback. I tried running some test data through this
model, but got initialisation failures, which forced me to realise
that I should explicitly truncate the lognormals from which I was
sampling. So now I have a statement like:

gap ~ lognormal(gap_self_mean, gap_self_stdv) T[latesttime
- prevtimes[k],];

I still get the warning, but I'm confident that stan performs the
appropriate correction. I can see why stan finds it hard to deduce, so
I don't worry. I get good results inferring on the test data :)

Thanks again -
Dan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Warning about transformed left-hand-side, in censoring model
parts:
You need the truncation bounds if gap_self_mean and gap_self_stdv
are parameters or if the truncations are parameters (latesttime - prevtimes[k]).
Otherwise, they're safe to drop.

I take it gap is guaranteed to be greater than latesttime - prevtimes[k]
by construction. Otherwise, you'll get automatic rejections.

- Bob
